Asha — thanks for the clear ask. High level we can do a staged canary with automatic rollback conditions. I've sketched an initial cadence and the network evacuation steps below; attaching a short checklist and a network drain diagram for NetOps.

Planned approach (summary):
- Canary 1: 1 control-plane host + 5% of serving capacity in isolated staging slice
- Canary 2: 10% serving capacity, smoke tests (latency, token errors, KV cache integrity)
- Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 10–15 minute hold windows and health checks
- Automatic rollback triggers: >= 3% error-rate increase OR median p99 latency regression > 50% over baseline OR failed KV cache sync

Network evacuation (edge steps):
1) Pre-drain: advertise reduced prefixes (BGP community) and enable local-preference shift to steer new connections to warmed nodes
2) Active drain: update eBGP to withdraw prefixes for canary pods via transit, maintain a small warm pool for control-plane RPCs
3) Quiesce existing long-lived connections using TCP FIN with a 30s drain; for persistent sessions provide a 302-style redirect to alternate endpoint (if client supports)
4) Post-cut: re-advertise full prefixes, validate flow through edge and return NAT mappings

What we need from Mercantile/NetOps:
- BGP neighbor maint window with router configs to set community tags for prefix throttling
- Access to a NetOps engineer on-call during the window (Slack + phone)
- Confirmation of traffic shaping/peak batch job schedule so we can set canary timing off-peak

Neha/Karthik/Soojin: looping you for ops/runbook details and to confirm rollback automation and KV cache handling.

Jonas
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Jonas — quick ops notes from the runtime side. Key clarifications to include in the runbook:

- Version pinning: we will stage v2.14.1-release (security build) behind a flag; runtime will keep prior 2.13.x pinned for instant revert. Document the exact model artifact hash and container image tag.
- KV cache safety: instruct that safe-sync must complete before traffic is shifted more than 25%. If sync fails, rollback immediately; this is currently implemented in the orchestration agent (ops-canary-controller).
- Tokenization and sequence-length regression checks: include synthetic prompt set (provided) and an automated diff of embeddings for sanity-check.
- Observability hooks: enable debug-level token tracer for the canary for 15 minutes post-cut to capture any subtle decoding regressions.

I recommend a narrow canary ramping schedule: canary-1 (00:00–00:20) -> hold 20m -> canary-2 (00:40–01:00) -> hold 15m -> full roll with 10m holds at 25/50/75%. That should fit a 3-hour hard window including remediation.

I'll attach the synthetic prompt set and a quick checklist for the team to sign off.

-Neha
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Asha / NetOps — adding network ops specifics from our side and a proposed acceptance checklist so we can sign the window.

Network acceptance checklist (proposed):
- BGP: confirm neighbor flaps are disabled for the window; establish community tag 0xFF03 to reduce prefix advertisement to 20% for canary slices
- Router configs: push config snippets via NetOps-API; NetOps must validate on a lab neighbor prior to live window
- Health probes: enable additional TCP health-check on edge 9091 (probe frequency 10s) during drain
- Fallback routes: pre-stage alternate path with higher local pref for control-plane RPCs so management plane stays reachable even if primary path drains

Operational gating for go/no-go:
- All smoke tests green for 15m across canary-2
- KV sync complete and no token-error spike > 0.5%
- External client simulation (Mercantile job replay) within expected tail latency

If Mercantile signs off on this checklist we can lock Nov 30 23:00–02:00 PST and I will open the change with our runbook and a single point of contact for rollback authorization.

Karthik
Head of Site Reliability
Redwood Inference
